explain.say: Sodium is a soft metal that fizzes in water. Chlorine is a poisonous green gas. Yet together they make the salt you sprinkle on your food! Look at the board. You start with a sodium atom, 2, 8, 1, with one lonely outer electron.

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a salt crystal lattice. Look at the sodium ion, the chloride ion and the ionic bond. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

explain.say: Chlorine is 2, 8, 7, just one short of a full shell. See the arrow? Sodium hands its outer electron straight to chlorine. Now both have full outer shells. Which one do you think is happier now?

explain.say: Both! But look at the charges. Sodium lost a negative electron, so it becomes Na plus, a positive ion. Chlorine gained one, so it becomes Cl minus, called chloride. An ion is an atom with a charge. Can you tell me which one is negative?

explain.say: Chloride! Now look at the magnet. Plus and minus pull on each other very strongly. That pull between opposite ions is the ionic bond. It forms between a metal and a non-metal. What do you think magnesium and oxygen would do?

faq.a: An ion is an atom or group of atoms with an electric charge, because it has lost or gained electrons. Losing electrons makes a positive ion; gaining them makes a negative ion.
A sodium atom has 11 protons and 11 electrons. When it loses one electron it has 11 protons but only 10 electrons, so it has a charge of plus 1.
asks: Why is a sodium ion Na plus?

faq.a: An ionic bond is the strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions. It forms when a metal gives electrons to a non-metal.
An ionic lattice is a giant, regular, three-dimensional arrangement of positive and negative ions, held together by strong ionic bonds in all directions.
asks: What is the structure of sodium chloride?

faq.q: Why does salt have a high melting point?
faq.a: Melting salt means breaking huge numbers of strong ionic bonds, which takes lots of energy. Sodium chloride melts at 801 °C.
asks: Why are ionic compounds hard to melt?

facts: In sodium chloride, each sodium ion is surrounded by six chloride ions, and each chloride ion by six sodium ions.
Ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or dissolved, because their ions are then free to move.

quiz.say: Magnesium (2, 8, 2) loses its outer electrons. What charge does the magnesium ion have?
quiz.show: Magnesium (2, 8, 2) loses its outer electrons. What charge does the magnesium ion have?
quiz.why: It loses two negative electrons, so it has two more protons than electrons: 2+.

wrong.1: Losing negative electrons makes an ion positive, not negative.
wrong.2: Magnesium loses two outer electrons, not one.
